mainTopic: Two rulings of שמואל seem to contradict each other on whether a person can forbid or consecrate something that does not exist yet (דבר שלא בא לעולם). רב יוסף resolves this by showing that קונמות work differently from הקדש.
overview: The גמרא finishes quoting a ruling of שמואל about a man who consecrates his wife's future earnings. There שמואל follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, which suggests that a person cannot consecrate something that does not exist yet (דבר שלא בא לעולם). This seems to clash with שמואל's ruling in our משנה that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The גמרא first suggests that שמואל only meant the point about the surplus (העדפה). It rejects this because שמואל would have said that more clearly. רב יוסף then answers that קונמות are different from הקדש, since a נדר can even forbid another person's produce to oneself. אביי rejects this, because in our משנה the wife forbids her future earnings to someone else, her husband. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע instead explains that she vowed on her hands, which already exist. The גמרא objects that her hands are pledged to her husband, answers that the vow starts only after divorce, and then asks how a vow can take effect at a later time like that, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling on consecrating a wife's future earnings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a case where a husband consecrates his wife's earnings. שמואל rules like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר that the surplus stays חולין. This implies a person cannot consecrate something that does not exist yet, which seems to contradict שמואל's ruling in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She may work and support herself from her earnings. As for the extra she earns beyond that, רבי מאיר says it becomes הקדש and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says it stays חולין. שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר. So it seems a person cannot consecrate something that does not exist yet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a source from elsewhere, where שמואל seems to hold that you cannot consecrate something that does not exist yet. This completes the challenge against שמואל's ruling in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife's future earnings do not exist yet when the husband consecrates them. If they stay חולין, the consecration did not take effect, so a person cannot consecrate a דבר שלא בא לעולם. That seems to clash with שמואל following רבי יוחנן בן נורי in our משנה, which assumes a נדר on future work does take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
Ordinary property, not holy
The surplus, what she earns beyond her needs
Apparently, this shows that
Something that does not exist yet

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different רבי יוחננs here. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר is in the source about consecrating the wife's earnings. רבי יוחנן בן נורי is in our משנה about the wife's נדר. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: She may work and eat from it.
phrases.notes: This is the wife whose husband tried to consecrate her earnings. She keeps enough to support herself.

phrases.english: And the surplus —
Rabbi Meir says: it is consecrated,
Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar says: it is non-sacred.
And Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar.
Apparently a person cannot consecrate
something that has not yet come into the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא אֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted source that the גמרא began citing just before this point, as a contradiction to שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the other source שמואל holds that one cannot consecrate a דבר שלא בא לעולם, yet here he seems to let a נדר take effect on future work.

steps.title: Suggesting שמואל only meant the surplus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way out: when שמואל ruled like רבי יוחנן בן נורי, he only meant the point about the surplus (העדפה), not the idea of forbidding something not yet in existence.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that when שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, he only meant it about the surplus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the contradiction: שמואל agreed with רבי יוחנן בן נורי only on one specific point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees with רבי עקיבא, so he seems to hold that the surplus belongs to the husband. If שמואל only agreed with that point, he never said a נדר works on future things. Then the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a suggested answer)
Surplus, extra earnings beyond what is required

phrases.english: And if you will say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי —
phrases.english: When he said the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri —
phrases.notes: "He" is שמואל, ruling on our משנה about the wife's נדר on her work.

phrases.english: it was about the surplus that he said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's ruling seemed to mean a נדר can take effect on something not yet in existence.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל only agreed with רבי יוחנן בן נורי that the surplus belongs to the husband.

steps.title: שמואל would have said so clearly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. If שמואל only meant the surplus, he would have used clearer wording, and he had three easy options to choose from.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let him say: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי about the surplus. Or: the הלכה follows the תנא קמא. Or: the הלכה does not follow רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 2 by listing three clearer ways שמואל could have said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain statement of 'the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי' sounds like full agreement, including his reasoning about future work. If שמואל meant only the surplus point, he would have said 'about the surplus,' or followed the תנא קמא who also holds the surplus is the husband's, or simply rejected רבי עקיבא. Since he did none of these, the answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him say (then he should have said)
Alternatively, or else
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי בְּהַעֲדָפָה.
phrases.english: Let him say: the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri regarding the surplus.
Or else: the halacha follows the first tanna.
Or else: the halacha is not like Rabbi Akiva!
phrases.notes: The word אֵין is in round brackets: some versions have it and some don't. Read with it, as here: שמואל could simply have said the הלכה is not like רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי בְּהַעֲדָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer offered in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that שמואל's ruling was limited to the surplus.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל's general wording does not fit a narrow meaning, because much clearer ways to say it were available.

steps.title: רב יוסף: vows are different from consecration
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that קונמות are different from הקדש. Since a person can use a נדר to forbid another person's produce to himself, he can also forbid something that does not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: קונמות are different. Since a person can forbid his friend's produce to himself, he can also forbid to himself something that does not exist yet.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first answer failed, רב יוסף gives a new answer: the rule about future things depends on whether we are dealing with a נדר or with הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With הקדש you can only consecrate what you own, so you cannot consecrate what does not exist yet. A קונם is not about ownership. It is about forbidding something to yourself, and that even works on someone else's fruit. So it can also work on things not yet in existence, and שמואל's two rulings no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Vows using the word קונם that forbid something
Since, because
His fellow's produce, which he does not own

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's idea: a person cannot consecrate (הקדש) something that does not exist yet, but a קונם is different because it forbids things to oneself without needing ownership. Watch the next step: אביי shows this does not fit our משנה, where the wife forbids something to her husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic difference between a נדר, which forbids an item to a person, and הקדש, which transfers ownership. That difference explains why each one can take effect on different things.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Konamot are different,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹת חֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו,
phrases.english: since a person can forbid his fellow's produce to himself,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹסֵר נָמֵי דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לְעוֹלָם עָלָיו.
phrases.english: he can also forbid to himself something that has not yet come into the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: שָׁאנֵי קוּנָּמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from steps 2 and 3 with a new way of resolving the contradiction in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both הקדש and נדרים should follow the same rule about things that do not exist yet.
steps.terutzMaskana: קונמות can take effect on a דבר שלא בא לעולם even though הקדש cannot, because a קונם does not depend on ownership.

steps.title: אביי rejects רב יוסף's comparison
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that רב יוסף's comparison fails. Forbidding another person's produce to yourself works because you control yourself. In our משנה, though, the woman forbids something that does not exist yet to someone else, her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Granted, a person can forbid his friend's produce to himself, since a person can forbid his own produce to his friend. But can he forbid something that has not come into the world to his friend? A person cannot even forbid his friend's produce to his friend!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב יוסף's answer from Step 4. He says the comparison to forbidding someone else's produce does not fit our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding another person's produce to yourself works because you have power over yourself, just as you have power over your own produce. In the משנה, the wife forbids her future earnings to her husband, so she controls neither the item (it does not exist yet) nor the person. Since you cannot forbid someone else's produce to that same someone else, you surely cannot forbid a thing that does not exist yet to another person.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense that... (sets up a contrast with what does not make sense)
Forbids another person's produce to himself
Something that has not yet come into existence
But (here it introduces the case that does not follow)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Forbidding a thing TO YOURSELF works even if you don't own it. Forbidding a thing TO SOMEONE ELSE needs some power over that thing. The wife in the משנה is forbidding to someone else.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, whose answer we saw in the last step.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא אָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹת חֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו,
phrases.english: Granted, a person can forbid his friend's produce to himself,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי אָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹתָיו עַל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: since a person can forbid his own produce to his friend.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא יֶאֱסוֹר דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לְעוֹלָם עַל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: But can he forbid something that has not come into the world to his friend,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹת חֲבֵירוֹ עַל חֲבֵירוֹ!
phrases.english: seeing that a person cannot forbid his friend's produce to his friend!
phrases.notes: He means someone else's produce forbidden to that same someone else. You control neither the food nor the person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's answer from Step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between קונמות forbidding another's produce to oneself and our case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison only covers forbidding things to oneself. Our case forbids a not-yet-existing thing to another person, the husband, which is weaker than even forbidding someone else's produce to that person.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: she vowed on her hands
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: the woman in the משנה said 'my hands are consecrated to the One Who made them.' Her hands already exist, so the problem of דבר שלא בא לעולם never comes up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: The case is where she says, 'My hands are consecrated to the One Who made them,' for hands do exist in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב יוסף's answer was rejected, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע offers a new way to explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining how one can forbid a thing that does not exist yet, he changes what the vow is placed on. The woman puts the vow on her hands, which exist right now, and the earnings are forbidden because of that. This avoids the whole problem of דבר שלא בא לעולם.

keyTerms.meaning: My hands should be consecrated to the One Who made them
They exist in the world
רב הונא son of רב יהושע, an אמורא

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common move in the גמרא: when a ruling seems to break a rule, explain the case so the rule never applies.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
It is where she says: "My hands are consecrated to the One Who made them,"
for hands do exist in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of רב יוסף with a new reading of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow was on her future earnings, which do not exist yet
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow was on her hands, which already exist, so דבר שלא בא לעולם does not apply

steps.title: Her hands are pledged to her husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer: how can she consecrate her hands when her husband has a claim to the work they do?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she said it like this, are they consecrated? But her hands are pledged to her husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's answer. Even if her hands exist, they are not fully hers to forbid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife's work is owed to her husband, so her hands are under a שעבוד to him. A person cannot consecrate something that is already pledged to someone else. So the new reading still does not explain how her vow works.

keyTerms.meaning: Are pledged / owed (under a legal claim)
But isn't it so that... (introduces a challenge)
Becomes consecrated

phrases.english: And if she said it like this, are they consecrated?
But her hands are pledged to her husband!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אָמְרָה הָכִי — קָדְשָׁה? וְהָא מְשַׁעְבְּדָן יְדַיהּ לְבַעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's claim that she consecrated her hands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her hands are under a שעבוד to her husband, and one cannot consecrate what is pledged to another

steps.title: She said it takes effect once she is divorced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that she made the vow start only after she is divorced, when her husband no longer has a claim on her hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where she said: When I become divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא's reading by adding a detail to the case: the vow begins only after a divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she is divorced, her husband's claim on her work ends, so the שעבוד no longer blocks the vow. This solves the problem raised in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: When I become divorced

phrases.english: It is where she said: when I become divorced.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a detail to the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her vow was meant to take effect right away, while her hands are still pledged to her husband
steps.terutzMaskana: Her vow takes effect only after divorce, when the husband's claim is gone

steps.title: How can a vow set for the future work now
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: right now she is not divorced, so how do we know a vow made today that only takes effect later is valid?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, at any rate, she is not divorced. And from where do we know that when she says it like this, it works?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 8 and asks for a source that a vow set to start in the future is effective. This sets up the next move in the סוגיא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment she speaks, her hands are still pledged to her husband. The vow would have to work later, at a time when she says nothing new. The גמרא wants proof that a vow can be made now on something that only becomes free to consecrate later.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, at any rate
From where (do we know)?
It is effective / it works

phrases.english: Now, at any rate, she is not divorced,
and from where do we know that when she says it like this, it works?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא מִיהַת לָא מִגָּרְשָׁה, וּמִמַּאי דְּכִי אַמְרַהּ הָכִי מַהְנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a vow set to begin after divorce is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When she speaks, she is still married and her hands are pledged. There is no known source that a vow made now can take effect later, once the thing becomes free.
